text:
sofia: Heads up — after last night's continuous-batcher heuristic tweak we're seeing a subtle latency wobble on a subset of pods. p95 jumped ~40ms on small reqs.
mike: saw that on dashboards around 03:17 UTC, throughput also dipped ~6% for the same flapping pool.
devon: did kernel routing change in the rollout? IIRC we switched the kernel affinity threshold for short sequences.
priya: yes, we lowered the shape affinity threshold to prefer small-kernel paths earlier. change landed 02:45.
sofia: logs show a brief kernel handoff churn where requests bounce between optimized_small -> fallback_fast -> optimized_small. that twice incurs extra context switching.
mike: can you paste the snippet from runtime logs? curious about the handoff markers.
sofia: sure — short excerpt:
```text
[02:46:12] request=tx=0xabc kernel_select: preferred=opt_small (shape=16)\n
[02:46:12] request=tx=0xabc selected=fallback_fast (reason=capacity)\n
[02:46:12] request=tx=0xabc migrate=opt_small<-fallback_fast (kv_tag=miss)\n
[02:46:12] kvcache: miss key=prefix-0xabc ret=MISS\n
```
devon: kvcache miss is interesting — did the heuristic change affect prefix bucketing? we might be invalidating prefetch windows more aggressively.
priya: the token-budget code was tightened too (target reduced ~8%) to favor latency SLOs. that combined with kernel fallback could be starving prefetch.
sofia: profilers from the canary show increased sys-time during the short handoff events. p99 tail moved ~110ms for ~2% of requests.
mike: canary-bot stats?
canary-bot: canary pool: qps=420 -> 395; p95=92ms -> 138ms; p99=210ms -> 320ms; kvcache hitrate=0.88 -> 0.73
devon: kv hitrate drop is the smoking gun. when the batcher lowers token budgets, it coalesces different prefixes into same window and invalidates prefetch assumptions.
priya: hypothesis: adaptive batch formation now groups a mix of short and mid sequences leading to kernel mismatch and evictions of prefetched KV entries.
sofia: agreed. quick mitigation options:
- revert affinity threshold (safe, fast)
- relax token-budget tightening (low cost)
- pin kernel routing to prefer opt_small if shape==short (safer)
mike: preference to flip affinity back for the fleet and run a narrow canary for the pinning change.
devon: i'll prepare a rollback patch for the heuristic flag (runtime.config.continuous_batcher.affinity_threshold) and stage to canary.
priya: i'll draft a short note for SRE runbook to watch kv hit rate + p99 and QPS delta.
sofia: nice. devon, can you also add a lightweight metric to emit "kernel_handoff_count" to help us count these churn events?
devon: yep, adding now. will push to canary at 04:05 UTC.
ci-bot: deploy queued by devon for canary group: run_id=deploy-24613579-c1
mike: monitoring — if canary stabilizes in 10m revert fleet roll or proceed with pin change. cc @priya for playbook.
priya: acked. I'll watch and escalate if kv hitrate < 0.80 or p99 > 250ms for longer than 5m.
sofia: update: after rolling the affinity rollback to canary at 04:07, canary-bot reports kv hitrate recovered to 0.86 and p95 back to 95ms within 3m.
canary-bot: canary pool (post-rollback): qps=422; p95=96ms; p99=215ms; kvcache hitrate=0.86
mike: good. let's hold fleet rollback until we validate two more canaries across different hw types (A100 vs L4).
devon: starting second canary (A100). patch note: keeping token-budget at tightened value for now to measure isolated effect.
sofia: long-term action items:
- adjust token-budget logic to be kv-aware (do not shrink budget below prefetch safety for mixed shapes)
- add kernel_handoff_count and add an alert when >0.5% of requests in 1m
- ensure batch formation respects prefix locality more strictly for short sequences
priya: will add to backlog and prioritize kv-aware token-budget as P0 for next sprint.
mike: thanks all. filing follow-up doc in eng-runtime wiki and we'll schedule a short retro tomorrow.
sofia: thanks — closing thread as canary looks healthy. will re-open if anything flares.
